about: One pace figure for the Budgets chip, /dubao, /month, the confirm warning and the agent's get_budget_pace (docs/02 section 2.11.2, A2). pace({ spent, limit, day, daysInMonth }) takes whole dong and the day of the month (1-based, today counts). null before day 5. Otherwise: daysLeft = daysInMonth - day + 1 (today counts); perDay = floor((limit - spent) / daysLeft), or null once spent >= limit (never a negative number); projectedEnd = spent x daysInMonth / day rounded half up to a whole dong, i.e. floor((2 x spent x daysInMonth + day) / (2 x day)) (Python: use // on ints, not round()); overDay = floor(limit x day / spent) + 1, the first day the straight-line projection is over the limit, or null when spent is 0, spent >= limit, or that day is after daysInMonth.

pace.name: A2 example: 7.100.000 of 8.000.000 on day 25 of 30
the same spending on day 4 gives nothing (a linear projection overstates early-month spending such as rent)
day 5 is the first day with a pace
over the limit: no daily allowance, never a negative number
exactly at the limit counts as over: no daily allowance
the last day: today's allowance is all that is left
spent 0: the whole limit over the days left, nothing projected
the allowance rounds down (3.000.000 over 22 days)
the projection rounds half up (5 over 10 days of 31 is 15,5)
the projection rounds to the nearest dong (100 over 6 days of 31 is 516,67)
February in a normal year: day 14 of 28
February in a leap year: day 14 of 29
the projection equals the limit exactly: not over
the projection is 2 dong over: over on the last day
the projection goes over right after today
a limit of 10^13 with 9 x 10^12 spent
less left than days left: the allowance is 0, not rounded up to 1 (99 of 100 on day 6)
